title: Public speaking
examples: What should I do if I forget what I was going to say?
How can I make my voice sound more interesting?
Is it okay to use notes when I speak?

explain.say: A good speech needs a clear beginning, middle, and end.
The introduction grabs attention and tells the audience what to expect.
Eye contact means looking at different people in your audience.
It is normal to feel nervous before you speak to people.

draw.text: Nerves: It is okay to feel nervous

explain.say: A real life example is giving a presentation in class.
A common mistake is reading directly from your notes all the time.

faq.q: How do I start my speech so people listen?
faq.a: You can start with a surprising fact or a short story. This helps immediately grab the audience's attention. You might also start with a question or a bold statement.
asks: What is a good opening line?
How do I get people interested right away?

faq.q: Should I look at my friends or the teacher when I speak?
faq.a: You should try to look at different people across the whole room. This makes everyone feel included and engaged with you. Try to make eye contact with several different faces.
asks: Where should I direct my gaze?
Is it okay to look only at my teacher?

faq.q: What if my heart is beating very fast before I speak?
faq.a: Take a few slow, deep breaths before you start talking. Breathing slowly helps to calm your body down. You can also pause for a moment when you get up there.
asks: How do I calm my nerves?
What can I do to feel less anxious?

faq.q: Does my voice need to be loud the whole time?
faq.a: No, varying your voice keeps people interested. Sometimes speaking louder or quieter adds emphasis. Changing your tone makes your message more engaging.
asks: Should I speak in one voice?
How do I keep my voice interesting?

faq.q: Do I need to memorize my entire speech word for word?
faq.a: No, memorizing everything can make you panic if you forget one word. Instead, remember the main ideas or key bullet points. This lets you speak more naturally.
asks: Is it better to write it all down?

facts: A clear structure helps the audience follow your ideas.
Making eye contact shows you are confident and engaged.
Deep breathing is a helpful technique for managing nerves.
Varying your tone keeps your audience listening attentively.

quiz.say: What is the best way to start a presentation?
quiz.why: This immediately captures the audience's attention and makes them want to listen.

wrong.0: This draws focus to your nerves instead of your message.
wrong.2: This is too common and does not grab attention right away.
wrong.3: This is boring and tells the audience nothing new.

quiz.say: If you feel nervous, what physical action should you take?
quiz.why: Slow, deep breaths help to calm your heart rate and mind.

wrong.0: Speeding up makes you sound panicked and unclear.
wrong.1: This makes you look uncomfortable and disconnected.
wrong.2: This can sometimes make your voice crack or shake.

quiz.say: When making eye contact, where should you look?
quiz.why: Looking at various people makes your whole audience feel connected to you.

wrong.0: Looking at objects instead of people seems unprepared.
wrong.2: This ignores the rest of the class who need your attention too.
wrong.3: This makes it seem like you are only talking to one person.
